summary: Kosei Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (PhD 1994) under Akira Hirakawa. He held posts at Waseda, served as associate professor at Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and was a professor at Komazawa University (~1999–2021).

Kosei Tada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a post at Taisho University and served as board chairman of the Society for the Study of Buddhist Culture (attested 2004).

Kosen Imakita was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Daisetsu Joen, Gisan Zenkai, Togai Fujisawa, and Kyokuso Hirose. He served as abbot of Eikō-ji (1858) and Engaku-ji (1875–1892), and worked at the Ministry of Religion (~1872).
Koshin Suzuki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a researcher (attested 1995–1998).

Koshiro Tamaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (DLitt 1959). He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1976), Tohoku University (~1976–1979), and Nihon University (1979–1986).

Kosho Kawamura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He held research and teaching posts at Toyo University through 1994.

Kosho Uchiyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a master's degree at Waseda University and studied under Kodo Sawaki. He taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary and served as abbot of Antai-ji from 1965 to 1975.

Koshu Itahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Teruji Ishizu. His education included studies at Sendai Daiichi High School, the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy, and Tohoku University.

Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Rissho University and as a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (both attested 2001).

Kotatsu Fujita was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. Supervised by Shoson Miyamoto and Hajime Nakamura, he served as a professor at Hokkaido University (~1969–1986) and former president of Sapporo Otani Junior College.
Koun Kajiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and later held a post at Taisho University.
Koyo Sakaino was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who held posts at Toyo University and Komazawa University, and founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1995).

Koyu Tamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as an associate professor at Toyo University (1972–2000) and also held posts at Nishogakusha University and the Encyclopaedia of Buddhism Department.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya was an Indologist who studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University. He held academic posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui was an Indologist who studied at Cotton University, Sanskrit College, Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as principal of Jagannath Barooah College (1930–1948) and vice-chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. Educated at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College under Alexander Duff, he held posts at Hare School (~1829–1832) and Bishop's College, Kolkata (appointed Second Professor 1852).

Krishnanath Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under teachers including Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2018, she served as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Colby College and Harvard under Anne E. Monius, Diana L. Eck, John S. Strong, and Charles Hallisey, later holding posts at Harvard, Brown, and Bard College.
